metadata.note: The Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton (Cincinnati and Hamilton RR chartered 2 March 1846; CH&D RR 1847; CH&D Railway from the 14 July 1895 consolidation with the Cincinnati, Dayton and Chicago and the Cincinnati, Dayton and Ironton) ran Cincinnati - Hamilton - Dayton from 18 Sept 1851 and, as lessee of the Dayton and Michigan from 1863, Dayton - Lima - Toledo, plus lines to Indianapolis, Wellston, Delphos and Fort Wayne. Sold at foreclosure 8 June 1917; its Ohio property became the Toledo and Cincinnati, operated by the Baltimore and Ohio from 18 July 1917. The core line kept B&O passenger trains (latterly the Cincinnatian) until 30 April 1971. Fourteen features: CH&D and B&O halves of Cincinnati - Dayton and Dayton - Toledo; a CH&D 1893-1906 span plus a 1914 anchor and a B&O 1927-1950 span on Hamilton - Indianapolis; B&O Indianapolis - Decatur 1942-1950; CH&D Dayton - Wellston 1896-1916; three CH&D one-year anchors (Delphos - East Mandale 1913, Deshler - Findlay 1913, Tontogany - North Baltimore 1901); and the separately-operated Dayton and Union, Dayton - Union City 1850-1931. Dayton - Delphos (1904-1913) and Findlay - Fort Wayne (1913) are researched but withheld: their grades are not mapped and would be mostly straight lines (see omitted).
metadata.ownership_split: CH&D -> Baltimore and Ohio on 18 July 1917 (ICC Val. vol. 42: T&C 'operated by the Baltimore and Ohio from July 18, 1917'; D&M likewise; DRHS says 19 July). Cincinnati - Dayton and Dayton - Toledo are each split into a CH&D feature ending 1917 and a B&O feature starting 1917 on identical geometry. NOT splits (same operator): CH&D RR -> CH&D Railway 1895; B&O stock control from July 1909 (and a 'part of B&O in 1912' catalogue date); receiverships 1905-09 and 1914-17; Henry S. Ives control 1886-87; the A&GW/Erie lease of 31 March 1869 and an Erie lease of Feb 1870 (ICC: own organization 1851-1895); the Pere Marquette combination 1904-05; USRA 1918-20. Hamilton - Indianapolis and Indianapolis - Decatur: CH&D as agent/lessee -> CI&W own organization 1 Dec 1915 -> B&O 1927; only the CH&D and B&O eras are drawn here. Dayton - Delphos: CH&D -> Dayton, Toledo & Chicago 4 Jan 1918 (not drawn). The Dayton and Union was never CH&D-operated and carries its own company and colour.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the research report's drawable: NONE: [5] Decatur - Springfield IL (no confirmable passenger year); [6] Sidell - West Liberty IL (no evidence; sold 1915); [8] Ironton Jct - Dean (no evidence; abandoned 1917); [9] Ironton Jct - Roads, Buckeye Branch and CD&I coal branches (freight); [15] Hamilton - East Middletown (no evidence; parallels the main line); [16] Troy - Piqua branch (no evidence; the main line already serves both towns); [17] Dayton - Soldiers' Home (no evidence); [18] Hamilton - Eaton - Richmond under CH&D control/lease 1866/69 - c.1886 (no confirmed CH&D-era year; recorded as an open Rule 4 question against the PRR feature in richmond_indiana_rail.geojson); the Lima Belt and Hamilton Belt (terminal roads). Also not drawn here: the CH&D era of Indianapolis - Decatur (a 1902 anchor is drawn in cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.geojson); the B&O eras of Dayton - Wellston, Deshler - Findlay, Tontogany - North Baltimore and Hamilton - East Middletown (no B&O-era passenger year; all freight-only by 1951); 1927-1941 on Indianapolis - Decatur (unconfirmed). Left to other research rows and NOT drawn here: the Dayton and Michigan's own years before the 1863 CH&D lease, incl. the ICC's 1859-1863 CH&D-operation claim (dayton_and_michigan_railroad); the CI&W's own operation of Hamilton - Indianapolis - Decatur 1 Dec 1915 - 1927 and its Hamilton - Cincinnati passenger trackage (drawn in cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.geojson); Erie through trains Dayton - Cincinnati over CH&D/B&O track c.1864-early 1930s (Erie layer); B&O Toledo - Detroit trackage (never CH&D property; a B&O-row decision). Not part of this report: the Cincinnati, Hamilton & Dayton RAILWAY interurban of 1926-30, a different company of the same name. Traced but withheld from the map at review (2026-10-29): 'Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton: Delphos Division (Dayton – Delphos)' 1904 [OPEN]–1913 [OPEN] and 'Findlay – Fort Wayne' 1913 [ANCHOR]. Neither alignment is mapped in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap for most of its length (Dayton – Versailles – Celina 57.1 of 90.7 mi, and 72.3 of 77.7 mi Findlay – Fort Wayne, would have been ruled straight lines), so they are left off until the grades can be traced (e.g. from historical topo maps). Delphos – East Mandale, which is traced, is kept as its own 1913 anchor.
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only years drawn. Every branch the Feb 1952 Official Guide marks 'Freight Service only' (Tables 57 Deshler - Findlay, 59 Hamilton - Indianapolis, 60 Indianapolis - Springfield, 67 Dayton - Chillicothe, 73 Dayton - Greenville - Union City) is drawn only to a sourced or last-confirmed passenger year, never to 1951. Freight lines (coal branches, belt roads, the Miami City Jct - Stillwater Jct stub after 1917) are not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_check: None: the CH&D and its narrow-gauge predecessors were steam from the start.
conflicts: Dayton and Michigan operator 1859-1863: ICC Val. vol. 42 says the CH&D operated the D&M 'from the date of its completion in 1859'; Wikipedia gives the perpetual lease as 1 May 1863 and DRHS control from 6 May 1863. Drawn from 1863; 1859-1863 left to the dayton_and_michigan_railroad row.
B&O operation start: 18 July 1917 (ICC) vs 19 July 1917 (DRHS). Year agrees.
CH&D opening: 18 Sept 1851 (Wikipedia, citing Warring 1887) vs 20 Sept 1851 reaching Dayton (DRHS); jjakucyk.com's 1846 opening is taken to be the charter year and not used.

Hamilton - Indianapolis B&O end: 1950 per chicagorailfan's Indianapolis page (drawn, the report's primary recommendation) vs the report's fallback 1927-1942 [OPEN] if that single secondary page is not accepted.
Junction RR sale to the CH&I: 2 Jan 1873 (ICC vol. 135 text) vs 2 Jan 1878 (its succession table) - affects when CH&D operation of Hamilton - Indianapolis began; not drawn either way.
Dayton and Union start: 'the first train was in 1850' (west2k) vs OpenHistoricalMap start_date 1852-04-26 on the D&U way. Drawn 1850 per the research report.
B&O control of the CH&D: July 1909 stock agreement vs a 'part of B&O in 1912' catalogue date - neither is an operating change.
Train name 1956-71: chicagorailfan lists Nos. 53/54 as 'Great Lakes Limited' in 1956 and 1971; Wikipedia says the Cincinnatian held 53/54 from 1950. Does not affect drawn years.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Open ends - each is the last (or first) CONFIRMED year, not a known end, and must not be extended without evidence: Dayton - Wellston 1896 [OPEN] - 1916 [OPEN]; Indianapolis - Decatur start 1942 [OPEN]. Hamilton - Indianapolis CH&D 1893 [OPEN] - 1906 [OPEN] (Fowler IN 71, added 2026-10-30). One-year anchors (service surely ran wider): Hamilton - Indianapolis CH&D 1914, Delphos - East Mandale 1913, Deshler - Findlay 1913, Tontogany - North Baltimore 1901. Hamilton - Indianapolis B&O end 1950 and Indianapolis - Decatur end 1950 rest on one chicagorailfan station page - confirm with a B&O timetable or an Indiana PSC discontinuance. Dayton and Union 1850 and 1931 rest on west2k.com only, and who ran its passenger trains is not established. Not consulted: Fowler's branchline.uk Ohio/Indiana/Illinois PDFs (unreachable 2026-10-29) - the most likely source for every branch's start and end; CH&D public timetables c.1880-1915. Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this file is an estimate. Byers Junction (start of the CH&D's own track south of Chillicothe) is not located.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line legs: 57.2 mi drawn against ~60 mi documented (ICC Val. vol. 42: the CH&D RR owned 59.74 mi Cincinnati - Dayton; the Toledo and Cincinnati 'about 60 miles') - about 4% short, consistent with starting at Cincinnati Union Terminal rather than the older depot further south. 53.7 mi runs on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O (CSX Toledo Subdivision, Cincinnati Terminal Subdivision) and 3.5 mi on untagged rail in the two terminal areas; it does NOT use the parallel ex-PRR/Cincinnati and Richmond line or the ex-Big Four line. Drawn mileposts: Winton Place 5.1, Hartwell 8.7, Glendale 13.1 (Lockland/Wyoming between), Hamilton 23.9, Middletown 35.3 (the line passes 1.1 km west of the town-centre geocode, on the west side of the Great Miami), Carlisle 42.4, Dayton 57.2. Every town waypoint lies within 0.4 km of the line except Middletown. ALIGNMENT ERA: the Cincinnati end is drawn into Cincinnati Union Terminal, opened 1933; 1851-1933 trains used the CH&D's own 5th Street / 5th & Baymiller station (jjakucyk.com), about 1 km to the south-east, so for 1851-1933 the last ~1 km is a later terminal alignment than the era. The Dayton end is drawn to the Union Station site (Sixth and Ludlow area, hand-pinned) on today's elevated alignment; the pre-elevation grade-level route through Dayton is not distinguished.

segments.note: The CH&D's trunk, Cincinnati - Hamilton - Dayton via Winton Place and Lockland/Glendale. First trains 18 Sept 1851 (two from Dayton met two from Cincinnati at Hamilton - Wikipedia, citing Warring 1887; DRHS says the line reached Dayton 20 Sept 1851). jjakucyk.com's 'opened between Cincinnati and Hamilton in 1846' is taken to be the 1846 charter misread and is not used. Cincinnati and Hamilton RR chartered 2 March 1846, renamed CH&D RR 1847, consolidated as the CH&D Railway 14 July 1895 - one company for Rule 4. Receiverships 4 Dec 1905 - 20 Aug 1909 and 3 July 1914 - 17 July 1917 were receivers OF the CH&D, not a change of operator; B&O stock control from 1909 did not change who ran the trains (ICC: 'operated by its own organization except ... receivers'). The 1869-70 Atlantic & Great Western / Erie leases are not treated as a split (ICC: own organization 1851-1895; see metadata.conflicts). Broad-gauge third rail laid 1865 for A&GW/Erie through cars, standard-gauged 1880. 1913: a CH&D 'theater train' left Cincinnati 11:25 pm for Glendale (PUCO 1913 complaint no. 31). END: the B&O operated the property from 18 July 1917 (ICC Val. vol. 42, Toledo and Cincinnati) - the 1917 boundary year is shared with the B&O feature. headway_min 120 is an ESTIMATE; no CH&D-era timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: start 18 Sept 1851 from Wikipedia CH&D (citing Warring 1887) and DRHS; end 17/18 July 1917 and the 'own organization' operating history from ICC Val. vol. 42 (Toledo and Cincinnati); 1913 theater train from PUCO Annual Report 1913 complaint no. 31 - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_hamilton_and_dayton_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-29). The headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [OPEN START AND OPEN END] 1893 and 1906 are the first and last CONFIRMED CH&D-era years, not known beginnings or endings. The CH&D ran this line "as agent" for the Cincinnati, Hamilton and Indianapolis "during its entire life" (from 2 Jan 1873 or 2 Jan 1878 - the ICC text and succession table disagree), then for the CI&W Railway (20 Sept 1902 - 30 Nov 1915; CH&D lessee 1 July 1905 - 30 June 1914) - one operator throughout. 1893: Fowler IN 71 z = 1893 Official Guide at Edgewood, Hanover, Ogleton, McDonald's, Griffin's (Mauzy), Farmington, Brandon, Lardona and Stratford. 1906: Midway, Donald, Salter's and Hurricane in the 1906 Official Guide. Fowler defines no later letter for this road, so 1906 is where the evidence stops, not where service stopped; the separate 1914 anchor (Connersville station) follows. The 1875 Guide stations (Fowler y) are not drawn because the 1873/1878 conflict leaves the 1875 operator unknown; if the CH&D start is settled as 1873 this segment can start in 1875. Do not extend without evidence. Through trains ran Cincinnati - Hamilton - Indianapolis. headway_min 720 is a placeholder ESTIMATE; no timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, Indiana Railroads SL 281, line 71 (z = 1893 Official Guide and 1906G station entries) for both years; ICC Val. vol. 135 for the CH&D-as-agent operation and the 1873/1878 conflict - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-30). The headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year only. The CH&D built Connersville's passenger station in 1914 (Wikipedia 'Connersville station') - the only CH&D-era passenger touch-down found on Hamilton - Oxford - College Corner - Liberty - Connersville - Glenwood - Rushville - Indianapolis. Service certainly ran wider both ways: the ICC says the CH&I was 'operated during its entire life by the Cincinnati, Hamilton & Dayton, as agent' (from 1873 or 1878 - the ICC text and its succession table disagree), then the CI&W Ry, CH&D-operated, 1902 - 30 Nov 1915 (CH&D lease 1 July 1905 - 30 June 1914). The 1893 and 1906 Official Guides (Fowler IN 71) confirm the earlier 1893-1906 segment; 1907-1913 remain unconfirmed and are not drawn. Do not widen without a timetable. The CI&W's own operation (1 Dec 1915 - 1927) is drawn in cincinnati_indianapolis_and_western_railroad.geojson. headway_min 720 is a placeholder ESTIMATE; no timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia 'Connersville station' (station built by the CH&D in 1914) for the anchor year; ICC Val. vol. 135 for the CH&D-as-agent operating history - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_hamilton_and_dayton_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-29). The 1914 station is weak evidence of service; the headway is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced, no long straight-line legs, but with five short bridged gaps and one stretch on another company's parallel track: 120.8 mi drawn against ~114.6 mi documented (ICC Val. vol. 42: 107.13 mi owned plus 7.52 mi B&O Southwestern trackage West Jct - Byers Jct) - about 5% long. DAYTON - XENIA (~20 mi): the Dayton and South Eastern grade, built narrow gauge, tagged old_railway_operator=B&O and now mostly the Creekside and Iron Horse trails (Kettering/Beavercreek), leaving the Dayton - Toledo line about 3 mi north of Union Station; four mapped-grade gaps of 0.29, 1.01, 0.15 and 0.46 km and a 1.23 km gap through Xenia (Xenia Junction / Detroit Street, where no B&O grade is mapped) are drawn as STRAIGHT LINES (about 2 mi in all). XENIA - WASHINGTON C.H.: B&O-tagged grade incl. the Jamestown Connector Bikeway. WASHINGTON C.H. - GREENFIELD (14.6 mi): drawn on the live ex-DT&I (Ohio Southern) track, which parallels the CH&D/D&SE line; the CH&D's own grade there is not mapped in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap, so this leg is corridor-accurate, not alignment-accurate. GREENFIELD - CHILLICOTHE: B&O-tagged track/grade (incl. 2.0 mi of the Paint Creek Recreational Trail). CHILLICOTHE - BYER - WELLSTON: B&O-tagged Renick Subdivision and lifted B&O grade (abandoned way named 'Cincinnati, Hamilton and Dayton Railroad' south of Byer). The ICC places the CH&D's own line from 'Byers Junction' and the B&O SW trackage west of it; the location of Byers Junction was not established, so the drawn Chillicothe - Byer stretch may run on the B&O SW main (Marietta & Cincinnati) for longer than the 7.52 mi of trackage - not resolved. Drawn mileposts: Xenia 20.1, Jamestown 31.5, Washington C.H. 49.5, Greenfield 64.0, Chillicothe 88.2, Byer 112.0, Wellston 120.8; every waypoint within 0.7 km of the line.
properties.documented_mileage: ~114.6 mi (ICC Val. vol. 42: 107.13 mi owned + 7.52 mi B&O SW trackage)

segments.note: [OPEN START AND OPEN END] The ex-Dayton and South Eastern (CH&D 'Ironton Division'), Dayton - Xenia - Jamestown - Washington C.H. - Greenfield - Chillicothe (West Jct; B&O Southwestern trackage to Byers Jct) - Wellston. CH&D operation from 1891 (Cincinnati, Dayton and Ironton acquired March 1891, operated by the CH&D - ICC), but the drawn span is only what passenger sources confirm: 1896 - the Xenia Gazette News-Current of 13 July 1896 says 'CH&D trains will stop using its depot on Main Street' for the new Detroit Street depot 'Xenia Junction' (west2k Greene Co.) - positive CH&D passenger evidence, though only at the Dayton - Xenia end; and 1915-16 - a union station shared with the B&O was built at Washington C.H. after the CH&D station burned in 1907 (west2k Fayette, citing the Record Herald), weaker evidence. 1896 is the FIRST CONFIRMED year and 1916 the LAST CONFIRMED year - neither is a known start or end; no source dates when CH&D passenger service on this line began or when B&O passenger service ended. Do not extend without evidence. The B&O era (from 18 July 1917) is NOT drawn: no B&O-era passenger year was found; Feb 1952 Guide Table 67 DAYTON AND CHILLICOTHE is 'Freight Service only' (Jamestown O. daggered '67t'), so passengers ended at an unknown date before 1951. The 1975 station closures (agency) and 1983 abandonment (DRHS) are not passenger dates. headway_min 600 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: west2k.com Greene Co. (Gazette News-Current 13 July 1896, Xenia depot) and Fayette Co. (Washington C.H. union station 1915-16) for the two confirmed years; ICC Val. vol. 42 (T&C, D&SE chapter) for the 1891 CH&D operation; Official Guide of the Railways, February 1952, B&O section (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt) Table 67 for 1951 freight-only - as read for research/branches/cincinnati_hamilton_and_dayton_railway.txt (researched 2026-10-29). Both ends are open; the headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] One proven year only, LOW. The Bowling Green Railroad (Tontogany - Bowling Green, 1874), bought by the CH&D in 1887 and extended to North Baltimore in 1890, via Portage and Rudolph. 'A new, larger CH&D combination station was built in 1901' at North Baltimore (North Baltimore Beacon, 8 Nov 1901, via west2k Wood Co.) - a combination (passenger + freight) depot implies passenger business that year. Service may have run wider both ways (the CH&D's 1894 Bowling Green station survives at Carillon Historical Park) but no other year is confirmed. The B&O operated the line until its 1978 abandonment - an abandonment, never a passenger end; no B&O-era passenger year was found, so that era is not drawn. The OCR-garbled 'arr. Bowling Green' line in the Feb 1952 Guide may be a bus connection and is not used. Do not widen. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line legs: 48.2 mi drawn against ~47 mi in the research report (not measured). Dodson - Arcanum - Greenville - Union City (35.1 mi) runs on OSM's lifted grade tagged old_railway_operator=B&O (incl. part of the Wolf Creek Trail); Dayton - Trotwood - Dodson (about 14 mi) runs on OpenHistoricalMap's 'Dayton & Western Railroad' way and the Wolf Creek Trail - i.e. on the Dayton and Western's (later PRR) track, which the D&U's trains used into Dayton (OHM's 'Dayton & Union Railroad' way, start_date 1852-04-26, begins at Dodson, not Dayton). That shared Dayton - Dodson stretch is also drawn by the PRR's Dayton - Richmond line in richmond_indiana_rail.geojson. Drawn mileposts: Trotwood 8.3, Dodson 16.2, Arcanum 27.6, Greenville 36.5, Union City 48.2.

segments.note: LOW CONFIDENCE, both ends approximate. The Dayton and Union Rail Road (ex-Greenville and Miami), Dodson - Arcanum - Greenville - Union City, reaching Dayton over the Dayton and Western. NOT a CH&D-operated line: the ICC (vol. 42) lists it as 52% Toledo and Cincinnati-owned but 'operated by [its] own organization', jointly controlled by CH&D and Big Four interests. START 1850: 'the first train was in 1850' (west2k Darke Co.) - one secondary source; CONFLICT: OpenHistoricalMap's 'Dayton & Union Railroad' way carries start_date 1852-04-26 (an OHM claim, source not checked). END 1931: the Greenville D&U passenger station 'went out of service for passengers in 1931' (west2k Darke Co.) - one secondary source. 1913 is independently confirmed: PUCO order no. 605 of 6 Aug 1913 names 'The Dayton and Union Railroad Company' among the four companies running passenger trains into the Dayton passenger terminal. Feb 1952 Guide Table 73 DAYTON, GREENVILLE AND UNION CITY is 'Freight Service only'. Who actually crewed the passenger trains (the D&U itself, the CH&D or the Big Four) is not established. headway_min 600 is an ESTIMATE.
